title: Sell Mineral Rights in Sidney, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Sidney, MT
metaDescription: Sidney, MT is the real center of Montana's Bakken, near the original Elm Coulee discovery. I buy mineral interests here based on actual decline curves.
heroLead: Sidney is the county seat and, honestly, the center of gravity for Montana's whole Bakken story.
intro: Elm Coulee Field, the discovery that proved the Bakken could be drilled horizontally at scale, sits right in Richland County around Sidney, years before anyone talked about North Dakota's boom. That gives Sidney-area mineral interests a real, two-decade production history behind them, not speculative edge-of-play potential. What it also means is that a lot of those original wells are mature now, well into decline, sometimes infilled with newer wells on the same unit. I evaluate a Sidney interest against that full picture, not against what a single royalty statement from a decade ago suggested it was worth.

The town itself grew fast through the 2010s boom years, and it's settled into a steadier rhythm since, which mirrors what's happened underground. I want callers from Sidney to have that same grounded expectation before we talk about their specific interest.

sections.heading: Mature wells, real decline
paragraphs: If your check has shrunk over the years, that's the expected shape of a horizontal Bakken well's life, not a red flag. I look at where the specific well or unit sits on its decline curve before I put a number in front of you, because that curve drives value more than anything else at this stage of the field's life.

sections.heading: Twenty years of leasing history to untangle
paragraphs: Sidney-area interests have often been leased, re-leased, pooled, and amended multiple times since the early 2000s. I pull the full chain from the Richland County Clerk and Recorder and cross-check it against Montana Board of Oil and Gas records before I make an offer, because a shortcut here is how a buyer ends up quoting the wrong number.

faqs.question: Is Sidney really tied to the original Bakken discovery?
faqs.answer: Yes — Elm Coulee Field near Sidney was the first large-scale horizontal Bakken play, discovered around 2000, ahead of the North Dakota boom.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check lower than it used to be?
faqs.answer: Most likely natural well decline. Horizontal Bakken wells drop steeply after their first few years, and that's normal, not a sign of mismanagement.

faqs.question: How do you handle a lease history that's been amended several times?
faqs.answer: I pull the complete recorded chain and cross-check it against state production records myself before making an offer.

faqs.question: Did the 2010s boom change what's under the ground, or just the town?
faqs.answer: Mostly the town and the pace of infill drilling. The underlying decline curve on the original Elm Coulee wells followed its own timeline regardless of the surface activity.
